cards.text: Pilate, the Roman governor, has handed Jesus over to be crucified, and the soldiers have taken Him away (John 19:16). Friend, this one is heavy, so stay close to me. Carrying His own cross, Jesus goes out to The Place of the Skull.

cards.question: The Place of the Skull, where Jesus goes carrying His own cross, has a Hebrew name too. In Hebrew it is called ___.

cards.text: There they crucify Him. And He is not the only one crucified there.

cards.question: Two others are crucified with Jesus, one on each side, with Jesus in the middle.

cards.text: Pilate isn't done yet. He has a notice posted right on the cross.

cards.question: Pilate's notice on the cross names Jesus of Nazareth. What does it call Him?

cards.text: Many of the Jews read this sign, because the place where Jesus was crucified is near the city.

cards.question: Many of the Jews read Pilate's notice on the cross. It is written in Hebrew, Latin and ___.

cards.text: The chief priests read it too, and they go to Pilate. They want the wording changed on a sign that's already up on a cross.

cards.question: The chief priests don't want Pilate's sign to call Jesus the King of the Jews. What do they want it to say instead?

answers.text: That He said He was King of the Jews
That He was a criminal from Nazareth
That He was a false teacher from Galilee

cards.question: Pilate gives in to the chief priests and changes the sign on the cross.

cards.text: Pilate answers, “What I have written, I have written.” Friend, that's not a reply. That's a door closing.
When the soldiers have crucified Jesus, they divide His garments into four parts, one for each soldier. But His tunic is left over.

cards.question: Jesus' tunic is seamless, woven in one piece from top to bottom. What do the soldiers decide to do with it?

answers.text: Cast lots to see who gets it
Tear it into four even pieces
Leave it at the foot of the cross

cards.question: John says the soldiers cast lots for Jesus' tunic to fulfill the ___.

cards.text: John points to the Scripture: “They divided My garments among them, and cast lots for My clothing.” (Psalm 22:18) And that is what the soldiers did.
Now look who's near the cross. Mary the wife of Clopas is standing there, and so is Mary Magdalene, one of the women who traveled with Jesus (Luke 8:1-2).

cards.question: Jesus' mother and her sister are also standing near the cross.

cards.text: Jesus sees His mother. And standing nearby is the one John calls the disciple whom He loved.

cards.question: From the cross, Jesus sees His mother with the disciple whom He loved standing nearby. What does Jesus say to His mother?

answers.text: Woman do not weep for Me

cards.question: Then Jesus speaks to the disciple whom He loved. He tells him that Jesus' mother is now his own ___.
From that hour, the disciple whom Jesus loved takes Jesus' mother into his home.

cards.text: After this, Jesus knows that everything has now been accomplished. And to fulfill the Scripture, He says, “I am thirsty.”
A jar of sour wine is sitting there.

cards.question: Jesus is on the cross, and a jar of sour wine is sitting there. How do they lift the wine to His mouth?

answers.text: On a sponge on a stalk of hyssop
In a cup on the tip of a spear
In a jar raised up on a ladder

cards.text: Jesus receives the sour wine. Then He speaks one more time.

cards.question: Jesus has received the sour wine on the cross. What does He say next?

cards.text: And bowing His head, He yields up His spirit. Sit with that one a minute, friend, because this story is not over.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'That He said He was King of the Jews', repeats the phrase 'King of the Jews' from the question. It is also the only answer about Jesus' claim to be king. The two wrong answers are general labels ('a criminal from Nazareth', 'a false teacher from Galilee'). A baker can pick the answer that echoes the question without understanding the chief priests' objection. The wrong answers should also be about what Jesus claimed or what He was called as king, so that none of them stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The blank asks for the third language in the list 'Hebrew, Latin and ___'. That is trivia about the wording of the list and adds nothing to understanding the passage. What matters in John 19:20 is that the sign was near the city and in three languages, so many people could read it. The card should ask about that meaning instead, for example why so many people read the sign.

rule.text: Ask about the moments that move the passage forward and the details the baker needs to understand it.

findings.problem: The card is only the fragment 'A jar of sour wine is sitting there.' It is a bare line from the verse with none of Papa Dorin's voice. It could carry the moment, or be joined with card 7 (Jesus saying 'I am thirsty'), which it follows directly.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
